title: Permissionless `createMarket` + External `borrowRate` Call Can Be Abused for Griefing / Gas-Grief via Stateful IRM Initialization
impact: `createMarket` calls into `IIrm(marketParams.irm).borrowRate(...)`. A stateful IRM (per the comment "Call to initialize the IRM in case it is stateful") may run arbitrary logic. Because `createMarket` is permissionless, anyone can front-run a legitimate market creator and create the market first (capturing no privilege, but emitting `CreateMarket` with identical params — actually the id is deterministic, so front-running just means the attacker creates the same market). The real risk: a buggy/stateful IRM could revert or consume unbounded gas on init, permanently blocking market creation for that IRM+LLTV combination if the IRM reverts deterministically for uninitialized state — but since any caller can retry, this is self-healing unless the IRM permanently bricks.
